profile.headline: Software Development Engineer III at Amazon - Game Engine & Developer Services
profile.summary:
Senior Graphics and Systems Engineer | Real-Time Rendering | Cloud Graphics | Cross-Platform Performance Optimization

Proven expert in real-time graphics and systems-level performance, with over a decade of experience driving innovation at companies like Amazon, Apple, and Cloud Imperium Games. Currently at AWS GameLift Streams, delivering low-latency, high-fidelity cloud-rendered experiences. Recently improved frame rate by up to 30% by optimizing GPU-CPU sync in the Vulkan capture layer and built out service monitoring from scratch to improve visibility and reliability.

Previously led key rendering initiatives in the Open 3D Engine, replacing legacy CryRender with a modern DX12/Vulkan pipeline and reducing CPU usage by 30%. At Apple, optimized Metal driver internals for iOS, boosting frame rate and stability in graphics-intensive apps, and supported third-party developers with detailed GPU performance analysis.

Deep experience with GPU architecture, rendering APIs (Vulkan, DX12, Metal), and cross-platform engine development. Known for combining low-level technical excellence with team leadership and open-source contributions. Commits publicly available under the handle rgba16f.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
Amazon GameLift Streams is a B2B cloud service that streams low-latency, high-fidelity graphics from the cloud to end-user devices. It enables scalable deployment of interactive workloads like multiplayer games, simulations, and 3D training.

•  Achieved up to 30% frame rate improvement by removing GPU-CPU sync points in the Vulkan capture layer.
•  Enabled team-wide visibility into service performance and customer issues by creating metrics-processing AWS Lambda and CloudWatch dashboards, where no prior monitoring existed.
•  Profiled the service, and the services on-instance binaries.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
Open 3D Engine (O3DE) is an open-source, AAA-capable 3D engine designed for real-time simulation and interactive experiences. Backed by the Linux Foundation, it supports photo-realistic rendering, modular development, and cross-platform deployment for games, virtual production, and industrial applications.

• Lead project to integrate Atom, a new DX12/Vulkan/Metal based renderer, replacing the old DX9/DX11 based CryRender. 
•  Reduced rendering CPU usage by 30% by parallelizing workloads and eliminating bottlenecks, improving real-time performance across platforms for a high-performance, open-source 3D engine.
•  Implemented features in the DX12/Vulkan/Metal backends of the new Atom rendering engine.

positions.title: iOS GPU Driver Engineer
positions.description:
Apple’s GPU Software team develops the low-level graphics drivers, performance tools, and rendering technologies that power visual experiences across iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Vision Pro. The team enables high-performance graphics and compute workloads by optimizing Metal, supporting third-party engines, and ensuring seamless integration between hardware and software.

•  Increased frame rate and stability in high-throughput mobile apps, as measured by internal benchmarks, by rewriting iOS Metal Parallel Encoder implementation.
•  Provided performance recommendations to third-party developers based on my analysis of their iOS graphics workloads.

positions.title: GPU Software Performance Engineer
positions.description:
•  Analyzed code, & characterized CPU & GPU performance of multiple third-party benchmarks.
•  Provided performance and quality recommendations to third-party benchmark developers.
•  Provided analysis of competitive third-party devices.
•  Analyzed performance of future hardware.

positions.title: Senior Programmer
positions.description:
Star Citizen is a massively multiplayer space simulation game developed by Cloud Imperium Games. It combines high-fidelity first-person gameplay with open-world exploration, dynamic trading, and real-time space combat across a persistent universe. Designed to push the limits of PC hardware, the game relies on advanced rendering and physics systems to deliver immersive, cinematic-scale experiences.

•  Prototyped a software meshlet virtual geometry approach to solve the game’s ultra-high draw count performance issues on DirectX11, increasing frames per second by 400%.
•  Educated the art team on the benefits of physically-based rendering and required content changes.
•  Enabled art team education and experimentation by fixing an early public revision of Crytek’s PBR technology.
•  Collaborated with the art team to evaluate desired new rendering features that DX11 enabled.
•  Sole graphics subject matter expert for all of C.I.G. and partner developers during 2013.
•  Mentored junior engineers.
•  Directed and evaluated work of external graphics contractors.

positions.title: Senior Engine Programmer
positions.description:
LightBox Interactive was an independent game studio known for developing Starhawk, a PS3-exclusive multiplayer shooter built in partnership with Sony, combining large-scale combat with real-time strategy elements.

Unreleased title
•  Rendering engineer on a small team creating a new PC & Playstation4 engine that supported realtime updatable art assets.
•  Created several render systems including a material (shader) system, a particle system, and related parts of the art pipeline.
•  Prototyped a Qt based level editor.

StarHawk, Playstation3
•  Created a system to manage non-interactive decorative objects (vegetation, rocks, etc).
    •  Managed 350,000 objects in 4MB of memory and less than 1 millisecond of SPU and CPU time.
•  Optimized GPU command stream generation by moving it to tasks running on the SPUs.
•  Took sole ownership of the runtime particle system and content pipeline.
